phases.title: Polish & deploy a production-feeling React + TypeScript case study
phases.description: Turn one strong deliverable from your Marblewood Health internship into a minimal but polished, accessible, tested, and deployed app demonstrating real impact. Focus on TypeScript correctness, accessibility fixes, test coverage, performance improvements, and a clear README with STAR bullets.

weeks.focus: Project selection, repo hygiene, TypeScript strictness & initial deploy
items: Choose one shipped internship feature or small app (user-facing UI) to turn into the case study; write a 1-paragraph goal and metric you’ll show (e.g., reduced clicks, improved load).
Create a fresh GitHub repo: convert code to full TypeScript strict mode (tsconfig strict), add ESLint + Prettier + repo README skeleton.
Set up branch + issue checklist (CI, tests, a11y, perf), connect repo to Vercel and make an initial deploy (document the URL).
Add a simple demo dataset or mock API so the app runs independently of Marblewood infra.
Run axe DevTools / Lighthouse a11y audit; fix top 5 actionable issues (semantic HTML, labels, keyboard nav, color contrast).
Write component/unit tests with Jest + React Testing Library for core flows (aim 60–80% on key components).
Add test scripts + coverage reporting; verify tests run locally and in CI (placeholder).
Update README with a short demo GIF, install/run steps, and a 2-line explanation of accessibility fixes.

weeks.focus: Performance, CI/CD, and impact messaging (STAR bullets)
items: Run Lighthouse perf; implement 1–2 wins (image optimization, code-splitting / dynamic imports, reduce bundle size with tree-shaking).
Create a GitHub Actions workflow: run lint + tests on push, and auto-deploy to Vercel on main branch.
Write 3 concise STAR bullets describing your internship impact (Marblewood Health) with numbers where possible — add them to README and your resume.
Polish README: tech stack, deployment link, short 'what I learned' section, and one architecture diagram (simple).

phases.title: Focused interview & on-the-job simulation practice
phases.description: Simulate the real expectations for a junior frontend hire: short coding tasks, React-focused take-home simulations, component-design whiteboarding, and behavioral STAR rehearsals tailored to startup health-tech teams in Austin.

weeks.focus: Timed frontend tasks and live-coding practice
items: Do 2 timed Frontend Mentor or CodeSandbox UI challenges (mobile-first) in 90–120 minutes each to mimic take-home tasks.
Solve 3 LeetCode Easy problems focusing on array/string manipulations commonly used in frontend interviews (use JS/TS).
Book 1 mock technical interview (Pramp or Interviewing.io) or a 45–60 min pairing session with a peer focusing on React component problems.

weeks.focus: Behavioral STAR prep and component design exercises
items: Refine the 3 STAR bullets from week 3 into 2–3 sentence spoken answers; record 5 common behavioral answers (teamwork, conflict, learning) and iterate.
Do 2 component-design whiteboard exercises: break down state/props/data flow, accessibility decisions, and test strategy; time each to 20 minutes.
Run through the deployed case study as a live demo script you can present in interviews (1–2 minute walkthrough).

phases.title: Targeted applications and networking in Austin
phases.description: Apply broadly but thoughtfully to junior frontend roles in Austin startups and health-tech, and activate local networks/referrals; prioritize companies likely to hire juniors and roles that list React+TypeScript and testing/CI experience.

weeks.focus: Submit applications, referrals, and interview scheduling
items: Apply to 10–15 junior frontend roles: use Built In Austin, LinkedIn (filter 'junior' + 'React' + 'Austin'), Wellfound (AngelList) for startups, Indeed, and Hired; tailor 1–2 resume bullets and 1-sentence cover note per application.

Message 8–10 Austin contacts on LinkedIn: former internship managers, Marblewood colleagues, Austin React meetup organizers, Women Who Code Austin members — share your deployed demo and ask for referrals or short chats.
Send follow-ups to any prior internship supervisors asking for a referral / short recommendation and permission to list the project on your portfolio.
Prepare an 'interview kit' folder: resume PDF, one-page project summary, demo URL, test coverage badge, and 3 STAR bullets to paste into online forms.
